scope: Undergraduate EE core courses including EE490 and EE492
introduction: The Undergraduate Electrical Engineering program reviewed its Course Learning Outcomes in Term 252 following ABET feedback concerning Student Outcome assessment. The previous curriculum mapping primarily followed the NCAAA learning domains. To strengthen outcome assessment under the ABET framework, the program revised the CLO structure to establish explicit alignment between Course Learning Outcomes, ABET Student Outcomes, and program Performance Indicators. As part of this review, selected CLO statements were modified, added, or omitted where necessary to support a clearer and more systematic assessment framework.

changes.old_clo_text: Recognize the main concepts of electrical parameters and their interrelations.
changes.new_clo_text: Explain fundamental electrical quantities, circuit elements, and basic AC signal concepts and their relationships in linear circuits.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze DC/AC electric circuits using Ohm`s law, Kirchhoff's circuit laws, and voltage/current divider rules.
changes.new_clo_text: Analyze DC resistive circuits using Kirchhoff’s laws, nodal and mesh analysis, and basic network theorems.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze DC/AC electric circuits using different analysis techniques such as Mesh, Nodal, and Thevenin.
changes.new_clo_text: Analyze AC circuits using phasor representation, including impedance-based analysis and power and power-factor concepts.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze sinusoidal signals, reactance, admittance, and power using phasor forms.
changes.new_clo_text: Investigate electric circuits through experiments and simulations

changes.old_clo_text: Demonstrate DC/AC electric circuits using hardware boards and simulation in group activities.
changes.new_clo_text: Contribute to team tasks and objectives in electric circuits laboratory activities
Evaluate ethical and professional responsibilities in electrical engineering design and analysis decisions

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze frequency selective circuits
changes.new_clo_text: Analyze frequency selective circuits, three-phase and two-port networks.
changes.note: Merged with baseline CLO 2.4 into revised CLO 2.3.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze three-phase networks and two-port networks.
changes.note: Content merged with baseline CLO 2.3 into revised CLO 2.3.

changes.new_clo_text: Acquire new circuit-analysis knowledge using appropriate learning strategies and apply it to solve circuit problems.

changes.old_clo_text: Demonstrate experimentally basic electronic circuits and their applications
changes.new_clo_text: Perform laboratory experiments on electronic circuits and analyze the resulting data to verify theoretical concepts.
changes.note: Renumbered from 3.1 to 2.2; domain changed from Values to Skills.

changes.old_clo_text: Describe the basic electronic circuits using diodes and transistors.
changes.new_clo_text: Solve fundamental electronic circuit problems involving diodes, BJTs, and operational amplifiers using principles of electronics and circuit theory.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze the characterstics of different BJT configurations and biasing circuits.
changes.new_clo_text: Design basic electronic circuits such as rectifiers, transistor amplifiers, and operational-amplifier applications to satisfy given performance requirements.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze operational amplifier characterstics and circuits for different applications.
changes.note: Operational-amplifier content was reorganized across revised CLOs 1.1, 1.2, and 2.1.

changes.new_clo_text: Explain the operation and applications of semiconductor devices and amplifiers using appropriate technical language and circuit representations.
Collaborate effectively in laboratory activities to build, test, and troubleshoot electronic circuits.

changes.old_clo_text: Describe different properties of continuous and discrete-time signals and systems.
changes.new_clo_text: Describe continuous- and discrete-time signals and systems using standard properties and classification criteria.

changes.old_clo_text: Recognize the sampling theory.
changes.new_clo_text: Describe sampling theory principles for converting continuous-time signals to discrete-time signals.

changes.old_clo_text: Explain Z- transform and its applications for LTI systems.
changes.new_clo_text: Analyze LTI systems using Z-transform concepts to interpret results and draw engineering conclusions.

changes.old_clo_text: Explain Continuous and Discrete-time Fourier Transform and its applications for LTI systems
changes.new_clo_text: Explain Continuous- and Discrete-time Fourier Transform concepts and their applications for LTI systems by interpreting frequency-domain results.

changes.old_clo_text: Write MatLab code and sampling theory and develop discrete system.
changes.new_clo_text: Write MATLAB code to implement sampling-based discrete-time systems and evaluate their performance using independently learned tools or functions.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze the selection, methods of speed control, and methods of direction reversal of and applications of d.c. machines
changes.new_clo_text: Design a DC machine and analyze its parameters.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze the selection, methods of speed control, and methods of direction reversal of and applications of a.c. machines
changes.new_clo_text: Design an AC machine and analyze its parameters.

changes.old_clo_text: Show the importance of sustainability in electrical machines and transformers
changes.new_clo_text: Acquire and apply new knowledge on electrical machines and transformers to engineering tasks.

changes.old_clo_text: Describe the types and operation of a typical microprocessors/microcontrollers.
changes.new_clo_text: Explain the functional organization and operation of microprocessor components including datapath, control unit, registers, ALU, and buses.

changes.old_clo_text: Explain the operations of peripherals typically used for interfacing microprocessors, such as A/D & D/A converters, Timer, Counters, LCDs, UART, PWM controllers, regular and stepper motors, Real time clocks.
changes.new_clo_text: Design arithmetic, logic, and timing components such as ALUs, registers, counters, and clock/timing circuits.

changes.old_clo_text: Illustrate microprocessor communication basics, hardware interfacing techniques, I/O addressing, interrupts, direct memory access, arbitration, and multi-level bus architectures.
changes.new_clo_text: Design control units and sequential systems using finite state machines for system control applications.

changes.old_clo_text: Demonstrate the ability to configure hardware and software microprocessor-based systems
changes.new_clo_text: Implement and verify an integrated digital system combining datapath and control components on FPGA hardware.
Model digital components of microprocessor-based systems using HDL at the RTL level.

changes.old_clo_text: Explain the concept of electric field and magnetic field.
changes.new_clo_text: Explain the fundamental concepts of electromagnetics, including electric and magnetic fields and their sources in free space and material media.

changes.old_clo_text: Analyze Maxwell’s equations to find the electric and magnetic field components in different media.
changes.new_clo_text: Apply Maxwell’s equations to determine electric and magnetic field components in different media and under relevant boundary conditions.

changes.old_clo_text: Develop an ability to apply Gauss’ law, Ampere’s Law, Biot-Savart law, Faraday’s law and Maxwell’s equations in the analysis of electromagnetic systems.
changes.new_clo_text: Analyze key electromagnetic parameters, including electric field intensity due to charge distributions, work and electric potential, electric current and current density, and magnetic field intensity.
Present an oral technical presentation on an electromagnetics application
Acquire new knowledge on an electromagnetics application using appropriate learning strategies.
Demonstrate effective technical communication of power system analysis and results.
Demonstrate the ability to independently acquire and apply new knowledge related to power systems.

changes.old_clo_text: Identify, gather and synthesize relevant information needed to define and solve an open-ended design problem.
changes.new_clo_text: Identify relevant technical information and engineering principles needed to define and solve an open-ended design problem.

changes.old_clo_text: Apply the engineering design process to define, formulate and solve a conceptual design problem considering human factors, safety, environmental, economic, and societal constraints.
changes.new_clo_text: Apply the engineering design process to produce solutions that meet specified needs with consideration of safety, environmental, economic, and societal constraints and relevant standards/codes.

changes.old_clo_text: Use lateral and critical thinking to generate creative alternative concepts and identify a preferred solution to a design problem.
changes.new_clo_text: Generate alternative concepts and select a preferred solution for a design problem.

changes.old_clo_text: Use engineering tools and drawing skills to check and visually communicate design problem-solving.
changes.new_clo_text: Communicate design solutions visually using engineering tools and drawings.

changes.old_clo_text: Communicate effectively and define engineering design problems and keep a well build log file and keep a journal of ideas and activities associated with the design project.
changes.new_clo_text: Communicate design solutions using written, visual, and oral technical methods.

changes.old_clo_text: Recognize the engineering profession and the importance of ethical and legal factors in professional duties
changes.new_clo_text: Evaluate ethical and legal responsibilities and their impact on engineering decisions.

changes.old_clo_text: Establish requirements, scopes, plan tasks, and meet objectives through effective teamwork.
changes.new_clo_text: Collaborate to establish goals, plan tasks, and meet project objectives within a team.
Validate design solutions through experimentation/testing, data collection, analysis, and engineering conclusions.
Acquire new knowledge, tools, standards, or technologies as needed to complete the design project.

changes.old_clo_text: Define and recognize complex electrical engineering problems encountered in industry, utilizing theoretical knowledge acquired in academic coursework to propose innovative and effective solutions.
changes.new_clo_text: Identify complex electrical engineering problems encountered in industry using theoretical knowledge acquired in academic coursework to propose innovative and effective solutions.

changes.old_clo_text: Examine advanced technical skills in electrical engineering, including design, analysis, and troubleshooting, to successfully complete assigned tasks and projects within cooperative work environments.
changes.new_clo_text: Apply advanced technical electrical engineering skills in design, analysis, and troubleshooting to complete assigned tasks and projects in a cooperative work environment.

changes.old_clo_text: Demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility
changes.new_clo_text: Demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility in engineering practice and decision-making.
Collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams to plan tasks, meet objectives, and support a professional work environment.
